scenes.text: It's a velvet ant. Not an ant at all, but a wingless wasp, nicknamed the cow killer.

scenes.text: In a 2018 study, lizards grabbed it and spat it out. Birds tried and gave up. A mole got stung and thrashed.
Its armour is so hard the predators couldn't pierce it, and it squeaks and leaks a foul chemical when grabbed.
Then there's the sting, one of the most painful in North America.
Only one animal swallowed a velvet ant: a toad. It immediately stopped breathing for a moment, and refused to eat another.

description:
Scientists fed this insect to lizards, birds, shrews and a mole, and it kept walking away.
Velvet ants are wingless female wasps. In a 2018 study in Ecology and Evolution, every lizard, bird and mole that attacked one gave up with the velvet ant alive: its exoskeleton could not be pierced, it squeaked, released a foul chemical and stung. Two shrews only injured one after repeated failed attacks. The only predator to swallow a velvet ant was an American toad, which briefly stopped breathing and refused to try again.
Which animal would you call truly indestructible?
first_comment: Five defenses in one bug: armour, warning colours, squeaking, a stink and the sting. Which animal would you bet survives anything?
